claim: Theme 4 requires early retrieval, multi-intent decomposition, fusion, stateful refinement, session-only memory and observable quality/latency/cost.
Acceptance gates include >=80% early retrieval, >=70% multi-intent handling, >=85% citation support and complete trace coverage.
Question decomposition followed by per-question retrieval and reranking can improve complex-query retrieval and answer quality.
RAG Fusion can improve raw recall without improving final top-k quality and can add latency.
Retrieval, generation and citation support should be evaluated separately; citation presence alone is not sufficient evidence of grounding.
Stable partial intent can trigger useful speculative retrieval before end-of-utterance.
Typed function signatures can provide validated model-facing tool schemas and runtime dependency injection.
Session, trace and nested observation structure can represent controller, retrieval, fusion and generation stages.
